title: More than one: -k, sok and numbers

sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: A noun becomes plural with *-k*, with a linking vowel after a consonant that follows harmony: *asztalok*, *székek*, *ajtók*, *lámpák*. After *sok* or a number the noun stays singular, and so does the verb: *Sok szék van itt.* *Mind* (all) goes with a plural noun and *vannak*. An adjective before a plural noun does not change: *a nagy asztalok*. After the noun it takes the plural: *az asztalok nagyok*.

items.spanish: A nagy asztalok és a kicsi székek.
items.english: The big tables and the small chairs.

sections.content: English says "many chairs", so it is tempting to write *sok székek*. In Hungarian the word *sok* already says it is more than one, so the noun stays *szék*.
